recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source edit is recommended because the requested guidance is already present and additional edits would duplicate or risk disturbing later published refinements.
issue_request: FHIR-13089 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core M&M issue asking to expand the old backward compatibility section into forward/backward compatibility guidance, including definitions, handling of new codes/resources/operations/references, unrecognized modifier codes, invariants and business rules, operation changes, CapabilityStatement/core IG additions, normative terminology exceptions, scope for core and HL7 International normative IGs, IG global profiles, conformance-resource reference changes, and a governance process for technically breaking changes.
initial_application: The historical application appears to be SVN-derived git commit fccd01d1da946ae8d270f20c68e2b6407b3b6dec, matching the Jira comment noting SVN #14685. That commit rewrote source/versions.html with forward/backward compatibility definitions, handling strategies, the compatibility rules table, operation wording, CapabilityStatement/IG/reference rows, terminology exceptions, and a rare technically breaking changes note.
additional_context: source/versions.html remains an active published page through publish.ini. Later published issues refined the same section: FHIR-24828 added the FMG breaking-change policy link, FHIR-36755 clarified warning/best-practice/error invariant language, and FHIR-38876 added the caveat that permitted non-breaking changes can still make some implementations fail. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-13089 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/versions.html already conveys the requested semantics: forward and backward compatibility are defined, older-system handling strategies cover unexpected elements/references/codes/search/URLs, the rules apply to normative core and HL7 International IG artifacts, and the detailed table covers new artifacts/codes/operations, value-set/code-system exceptions, invariants, CapabilityStatements, global profiles, and conformance-resource references.

related_jiras.note: Added the FMG breaking-change policy reference now present in the same compatibility rules section.
Clarified warning, best-practice, and error invariant language in the same value-constraints row.
Added the current caveat that compatibility rules do not guarantee old implementations will keep working.
